solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stalwart of space programme? Well, his Martian is fluent

indicators.note: fluent here means flowing freely, so the letters of the preceding words run into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone praises an astronaut whose Martian language is impressively fluent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'space programme' is a TV one: William Shatner played Captain Kirk in Star Trek, the anagram of WELL HIS MARTIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor was the leading figure of the Star Trek television series, a programme set in space.

clue.text: Sitting in VW, I personally use these in wet weather

definitions.text: Sitting in VW, I personally use these in wet weather

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words, so they conceal it

explanation.surface: A driver in a Volkswagen explains what they switch on when it rains.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is concealed across 'VW, I personally', and the whole clue doubles as its definition: a driver in a car uses wipers in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Windscreen blades are switched on by a motorist to clear rain from the glass.

clue.text: Spraying toilet with Vim is a repetitive theme

indicators.note: spraying scatters things about, so the letters of the following words are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; Vim is a brand of cleaning powder

explanation.surface: Cleaning the lavatory with Vim cleanser becomes a dreary recurring routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Vim is a British brand of scouring powder; 'with' only joins the two words being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical or literary motif associated with a character or idea.

clue.text: This month start to activate social network, as the kids say

definitions.text: social network, as the kids say

parts.note: inst. (instant) is an old commercial abbreviation for this month

indicators.note: the start of the next word means its first letter only

explanation.surface: Young people urge signing up to a social media platform this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' is old business-letter shorthand for 'of this month', as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insta is the young people's slang shortening of Instagram, the photo-sharing platform.

clue.text: Foolish schoolmarm reportedly took the lead

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the words before and after are spoken aloud

parts.note: a female schoolteacher is addressed as Miss
to guide is to lead the way, so took the lead means guided

explanation.surface: A daft schoolteacher apparently went out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes MISS, said aloud, stand for MIS; spoken together, MISS GUIDED sounds exactly like the single word for unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Misguided describes judgement that is unwise or mistaken, as a foolish action is.

clue.text: See 1
Small step where Armstrong was?

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A nod to Neil Armstrong's famous small step on the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'one small step for man'; Armstrong travelled through outer space to reach the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong flew through outer space as an astronaut, so space is his location in the question.

clue.text: New camera has this gold, soft alloy lined with old copper

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: lined with means having something inside, so the second piece goes within the first
an alloy is a blend of metals, so the letters of the preceding word are blended

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A camera made of gold and a soft alloy with copper in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alloy' looks like part of the metallurgy but is the anagram signal, making TOFS; 'lined with' then puts the old copper inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Autofocus is a feature of modern cameras that sharpens the image automatically.

clue.text: New year, on one's tod, unwrapped something found in stocking

indicators.note: unwrapped means the outer covering is removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: on one's tod is British rhyming slang (Tod Sloan) for alone

explanation.surface: Someone spending New Year alone opens a present from their Christmas stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On one's tod' is British rhyming slang for alone (Tod Sloan, a jockey); 'unwrapped' strips ALONE to LON. The stocking is hosiery, not a Christmas one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is the synthetic fibre that women's stockings are typically made from.

clue.text: Having remembered name, actor Oliver comes round

indicators.note: comes round means surrounds, so the actor's surname goes around the other piece

parts.note: Oliver Reed was an English film actor
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: The actor Oliver Reed regains consciousness and recalls a name.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Reed was a hell-raising English film actor; 'comes round' suggests waking up but here means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalled is the past participle of recall, meaning brought back to mind or remembered.

clue.text: Father, taking temperature, sticks his nose in

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a Catholic priest is addressed as Father

explanation.surface: A meddlesome priest takes someone's temperature and pokes into their business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like it should add T, but here it means taking it away from PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To pry is to inquire nosily into others' affairs, which matches sticking one's nose in.

clue.text: Clever clogs regularly sampling some craft beer, cold

indicators.note: taking a regular sample means picking alternate letters from the next word

parts.note: craft means skill or art
ale is a kind of beer
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A know-all tastes some craft beer served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly sampling' takes alternate letters of 'some', giving SM; craft, beer and cold then supply the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever clogs is a British informal term for a know-all, as is smart alec.

clue.text: Once again assess tons pinched from treasure Julius buried

indicators.note: buried means placed within, so the setter's pronoun goes inside the remaining letters
pinched from means stolen away, so the letter is removed from the next word

parts.note: Julius is the setter, so the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter buries treasure after some of it was stolen, and takes stock again.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves, here Julius, to mean the first-person pronoun; 'pinched from' removes the tons abbreviation, leaving REASURE, and 'buried' puts the pronoun inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To remeasure is to measure again, and measuring is a form of assessing size or amount.

clue.text: Last bit of fish, half skinned

parts.note: a fin is a part of a fish

indicators.note: skinned means the outer layer is removed, so the first and last letters of the word go

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a fish, half of it skinned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' is not a halving instruction: the word HALF itself is skinned to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Final means coming at the end, the very last in a series.

clue.text: One who nicks those nicking knickers?

definitions.text: One who nicks those nicking knickers?

parts.words: One who nicks those nicking knickers?
parts.note: nick is British slang both for arrest and for steal, so this describes a shop's security officer catching underwear thieves

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone catching thieves of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' in British slang means both to arrest and to steal; the person arresting shoplifters is a plain-clothes security officer in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A store detective is employed to catch shoplifters, such as those stealing lingerie.

clue.text: Turkey entering dispute supporting Rhode Island strong drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below, so this piece comes after the state

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the country code goes into the dispute

parts.note: a set-to is a quarrel or dispute
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Turkey joins an argument backing Rhode Island over a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' makes STRETTO, and in a down entry 'supporting' means sitting below the state abbreviation. A ristretto is an Italian coffee, not alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A ristretto is a very short, concentrated shot of espresso coffee, a strong drink.

clue.text: Those running a fast time in stretch of tidal water

indicators.note: running here means flowing loosely, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Athletes clocking a quick time in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fast time' looks like a quick race time but is the period of fasting, LENT; 'running' rearranges THOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland southern England.

clue.text: One very still, regarding the equilibrium in the earth's crust

definitions.text: regarding the equilibrium in the earth's crust

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so means very, as in so good
static means still or not moving

explanation.surface: A person keeping perfectly still talks about geology.
explanation.definitionFit: Isostatic relates to isostasy, the balance by which the earth's crust floats on the denser mantle.

clue.text: Border row after the majority of Norfolk gets upset

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the row is placed behind the reversed county letters
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
the majority of a word means most of its letters, so the end is cut off

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A boundary dispute in Norfolk upsets most of the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the majority of' Norfolk is NORF, which 'gets upset' turns into FRON; 'after' puts the row after it. Norfolk is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the boundary line between two countries, a border.

clue.text: I've served 20 different ministers devoted to this work

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: the answer to clue 20 across, the exclamation of refusal

explanation.surface: A retired cleric looks back on serving under a refusal-filled career.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross-referenced 20 gives NO SIR, and 'different' rearranges it with I'VE SERVED. The definition describes the 1880s English Bible revision clergy worked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Revised Version is the 19th-century revision of the King James Bible, which ministers read and preach from.

clue.text: Caught husband trafficking gear for a price

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: trafficking means dealing about illicitly, so the letters of the next word are moved around

explanation.surface: A husband is arrested for dealing in drugs for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' is slang for drugs, which fits the surface; 'trafficking' rearranges it to ARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price asked for goods or a service.

clue.text: More inquisitive European deported? Certainly not!

indicators.note: deported means sent away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: nosier means more inquisitive

explanation.surface: A nosy European is expelled and someone flatly refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: No sir is an emphatic refusal, the same as an indignant certainly not.

clue.text: Those spreading the gospel about old pediatrician

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the society's initials go around the letter

parts.note: the SPCK is the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge

explanation.surface: Missionaries discussing a children's doctor from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The SPCK is the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, an Anglican missionary publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Spock was the American paediatrician whose baby-care book was a worldwide bestseller.

clue.text: One is used to time spinner cutting sample of cloth

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the toy goes inside the cloth sample

parts.note: a swatch is a small sample of fabric
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A tailor's sample is sliced by a spinning device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler, but it is the spinning toy, TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch is a handheld timer used to measure elapsed time, as in races.

clue.text: Begin long-running TV series killing off Queen, Earl & King

indicators.note: killing off characters means removing them, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: Star Trek is the long-running science-fiction TV franchise
R (Regina) is the standard abbreviation for queen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A soap opera writes out a queen, an earl and a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The series is Star Trek, from which REK is removed; it links to William Shatner at 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to begin, commence or set something going.

clue.text: At which point wife's present

parts.note: here means present, as in a register

explanation.surface: Asking at what moment a wife turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Where can mean at which place or stage, as in 'the scene where he dies'.

clue.text: Odd redaction doesn't bother me

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of the next word are in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a strange piece of censorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying I don't care declares indifference, that something is of no concern to the speaker.

clue.text: Make an appearance, always poetically holding part of the 18?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the poetic word goes around the other piece

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
NT, the New Testament, is part of the Revised Version Bible at 18 across

explanation.surface: An actor makes an entrance, quoting scripture poetically.
explanation.walkthrough: The 18 is the Revised Version of the Bible, of which the New Testament (NT) is a part.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come on stage or into a room, appearing before others.

clue.text: Chapter from Kerouac pulped — time to get rid of the leaves

indicators.note: pulped means mashed up, so the letters are rearranged once the chapter letter is removed

parts.note: the surname of the Beat writer, taken as written

explanation.surface: A chapter of a Jack Kerouac novel is pulped, as books' pages are destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks C as taken out of KEROUAC, and 'pulped' rearranges the rest to RAKEOU; 'leaves' sounds like book pages but means fallen foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake out is to clear something away with a rake, as gardeners do with fallen foliage.

clue.text: Sticky stuff Marcel every so often covered with ash?

indicators.note: covered with means enclosed, so the picked letters sit inside the tree

parts.note: the ash is a kind of tree

indicators.note: every so often means at regular intervals, so alternate letters of the name are picked

explanation.surface: Marcel is occasionally coated in a sticky residue, perhaps from cigarette ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ash' looks like cigarette ash but is the tree; 'every so often' takes ACL from Marcel.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick, sticky syrup made in refining sugar, like molasses.
